method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

sourceChecks.note: Primary provider guidance retrieved: compressed bulb creates suction; check secure closure; measure each drain separately; secure tubing and monitor problems. Device-specific instructions remain necessary.

Primary toolkit opened: monitor outflow to prevent overdistension and identify obstruction; proposed explicit pause of inflow reflects obstruction safety principle, local protocol governs subsequent manual actions.
Primary ACI guidance retrieved: collection system stays below chest level.

Primary ACI troubleshooting retrieved: continuous bubbling suggests leak and cessation with symptoms needs patient/system assessment. Brief protocol-directed diagnostic clamping is distinct from leaving a tube clamped.

items.assessment: New swelling makes stopped output concerning rather than a removal criterion; prompt tubing/site assessment is uniquely appropriate. No invasive manipulation is prescribed.

An immediate loss of bulb compression suggests a seal/connection problem. Device-instruction check is more appropriate than unsupported wall suction or dressing change alone; primary MSK guidance supports the mechanism.
Key is accurate but all alternatives are conspicuously inaccurate documentation. Use realistic aggregation/measurement shortcuts.
issues: Key is accurate but all alternatives are conspicuously inaccurate documentation. Use realistic aggregation/measurement shortcuts.

options: Record the combined volume and describe the overall colour
Record each volume but use one colour description for both
Record each colour and estimate volumes from bulb fullness
Measure and describe each drain separately
why: Combining obscures which operative area produced the change.
Each drain has a distinct appearance that should remain attributable to that drain.
Measure each volume; bulb fullness is not a reliable substitute for measurement.
Site-specific trends can identify which area has changed.

items.assessment: The mismatch between visible stain and dependent blood is useful application: assess hidden loss and circulation before linen care or local reinforcement. Options are coherent competing priorities.

issues: Current loss/replacement is correct but the two only-options are obvious and remote meal history is filler. Use comparable clinically relevant histories.

Mouth-care frequency and the effect on reported thirst

items.assessment: Increasing distension contradicts assuming recovery; position indicators/patency assessment per policy is appropriately scoped. Feeding, clamping and pressure escalation are recognizable decompression errors.
Visible kink is an immediately correctable mechanical cause; reassessment after release precedes catheter replacement or diagnostic escalation. No general assessment-first rule blocks correction.
Question asks for assessment but option0 is fluid restriction. Remove action/category mismatch and only qualifiers.
issues: Question asks for assessment but option0 is fluid restriction. Remove action/category mismatch and only qualifiers.

Small voids can coexist with substantial retained urine.
Appearance does not establish whether the bladder emptied.
Frequency alone cannot distinguish small complete voids from retention.

items.assessment: 1650 minus1200 equals450mL; alternatives map to specific input/output arithmetic errors. Math is meaningful, assumes same interval and no other fluid, and does not authorize administration.
Assessment/protocol wording is too vague about ongoing inflow when drainage is obstructed. State stopping inflow while addressing obstruction; avoid a routine bag-change distractor.
issues: Assessment/protocol wording is too vague about ongoing inflow when drainage is obstructed. State stopping inflow while addressing obstruction; avoid a routine bag-change distractor.

Give the prescribed antispasmodic and then reassess drainage
Lower the irrigation bag to slow inflow until the next observation
Pause irrigation inflow, assess outflow, and follow the obstruction protocol

Symptoms may reflect obstructed outflow; symptom treatment must not delay checking drainage.
Reducing flow alone does not establish that outflow is safe.
Continuing inflow with impaired drainage can overdistend the bladder; act on patency and escalate per protocol.

items.assessment: Above-chest collection and compressed tubing require correction; upright unit and secure connections are appropriate. Primary ACI drainage guidance supports dependent unobstructed positioning.

issues: The new continuous water-seal bubbling is a good cue, but ignore-all-bubbling is cartoonish. Replace with misidentification of the chamber mechanism.

Clamp the tube and leave it clamped

items.assessment: Worsening breathlessness prevents interpreting abrupt drainage cessation as recovery. Urgent patient/system assessment is the priority; primary ACI troubleshooting supports obstruction checks and escalation.

issues: The SATA is clinically sound but rolled sleeves at ankles is too conspicuous. Substitute a familiar fit shortcut.

Sleeves fit according to device instructions

Sizing must match the client and device instructions; a universal oversize can impair intended compression.

Correct fit supports intended compression without excessive pressure.

items.assessment: Other-client stocking is an implausible/unethical filler distractor. Make it a plausible unilateral prophylaxis escalation error.
issues: Other-client stocking is an implausible/unethical filler distractor. Make it a plausible unilateral prophylaxis escalation error.

items.assessment: Slow inhalation corrects the observed technique error. Rapid inhalation, forced exhalation and desaturation-only use represent relevant misconceptions. Foundation skill is clearly scoped to an ordered device.

issues: Repeated room moves for convenience and continuous darkness are weak distractors. Use realistic attempts to reduce stimulation.
